sections.title: Overview
sections.body: We previously learned how to create an MCP server and client. Now we will examine what happens at the protocol level.

steps.label: Goal
steps.narration: The agent receives a user goal and must decide what information or tools are required.

steps.label: Reason
steps.narration: The model plans the next action instead of answering blindly.

steps.label: Act / tool
steps.narration: The agent calls an authorized tool or function with structured arguments.

steps.label: Observe
steps.narration: Usage, cost, latency, and traces are recorded for FinOps and incident response.

steps.label: Decide
steps.narration: The loop continues, escalates to a human, or finishes with a grounded answer.

scenario.title: Scenario — Part — 42. Advanced MCP protocol engineering
scenario.situation: tool invocation: json { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 42, "method": "tools/call", "params": { "name": "get_invoice", "arguments": { "invoice_id": "INV-101" } } } The request ID correlates a protocol request with its response. It is not a business transaction idempotency key.

choices.label: Ignore it and ship anyway
choices.explanation: Skipping detection leaves users exposed and makes root-cause analysis harder later.

choices.label: Add detection signals first
choices.explanation: Instrument logs, metrics, and traces that reveal this failure mode.

choices.label: Apply a production fix / mitigation
choices.explanation: Apply layered mitigations, validate with tests, and monitor recovery.

sections.title: 42.1 MCP communication lifecycle
sections.body:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as MCP Client
    participant S as MCP Server
    C->>S: initialize
    S-->>C: Protocol version and capabilities
    C->>S: notifications/initialized
    C->>S: tools/list
    S-->>C: Tool definitions
    C->>C: Validate and select capabilities
    C->>S: tools/call
    S-->>C: Structured result or error
```

This is the familiar MCP JSON-RPC lifecycle. Production clients should negotiate compatible protocol versions and supported capabilities rather than assuming all servers implement identical features.

sections.title: 42.2 JSON-RPC request structure
42.3 Transports
sections.body:
| Transport | Typical use |
|--------|--------|
| stdio | Local subprocess integrations |
| Streamable HTTP | Remote client-server communication |
| Older HTTP/SSE implementations | Compatibility with older protocol deployments |

Transport selection affects authentication, connection lifecycle, session handling, scaling and recovery.

A local stdio MCP server is executable software. Installing one should be treated as a software supply-chain decision.

sections.title: 42.4 Important MCP engineering considerations
sections.body:
Tool lists may be paginated or updated. Clients must handle compatible capability changes, request deadlines, disconnections, structured result validation and protocol errors.

Where HTTP authorization is used, follow the authorization requirements of the negotiated specification, including resource-specific credentials and appropriate token validation. citeturn505501search20turn505501search28
